abstract_algebra: Covers abstract algebra broadly, including group theory (subgroups, cosets, cyclic groups, homomorphisms, and related theorems), ring theory, and field theory. Frequently involves proving or evaluating statements about algebraic structures and their properties, as well as direct computation on groups, rings, and fields. Does not cover elementary arithmetic, calculus, or applied mathematics.
anatomy: Covers human anatomical structure and function broadly, including body systems such as cardiovascular, respiratory, nervous, musculoskeletal, and lymphatic anatomy, as well as embryological development. Frequently involves identifying structural locations, connections between anatomical parts, and normal physiological mechanisms. Does not cover disease diagnosis, treatment, or clinical pathology.
astronomy: Covers astronomy and astrophysics broadly, including celestial bodies (planets, stars, and their properties), stellar and galactic phenomena (luminosity, distance measurement, heat generation), subatomic particles relevant to astrophysics, and astronomical instrumentation such as telescopes. Frequently involves identifying physical mechanisms, approximate quantities, and observational techniques used in studying the universe. Does not cover Earth-based geology, biology, or terrestrial physics unrelated to celestial contexts.
